_comment: Interview probes, portfolio project ideas and first steps, per skill. 'clusters' is the fallback used when a skill has no bespoke entry, so every skill in the gazetteer yields role-appropriate content. Probes are written to be unanswerable from the resume alone: they ask how, not whether.

Frontend.probe: Walk me through a component you built that turned out harder than expected. What made it hard?
Frontend.project: Rebuild one screen of a product you use, matching its behaviour on mobile and desktop.
Frontend.first_step: Ship one small interface and get it working on a phone as well as a laptop.

Backend.probe: Take an endpoint you have written and walk me through what happens between the request arriving and the response leaving.
Backend.project: Build a small API with authentication, persistence and a documented set of endpoints.
Backend.first_step: Build one CRUD API end to end and document its endpoints in the README.

Database.probe: Describe a schema you designed. What would you change about it now?
Database.project: Model a real domain (bookings, inventory, a library) and write the queries the app would need.
Database.first_step: Design one schema with at least three related tables and write the joins yourself.

DevOps.probe: How does your code get from your laptop to somewhere another person can use it?
DevOps.project: Take an existing project of yours and give it a reproducible deployment and an automated build.
DevOps.first_step: Containerise one project you have already built and deploy it somewhere public.

Fundamentals.probe: Tell me about a bug that took you more than a day. How did you find it?
Fundamentals.project: Solve a problem end to end in an unfamiliar language and write up what transferred.
Fundamentals.first_step: Work through a structured problem set and write up your reasoning, not just the answer.

Data.probe: Describe a dataset you worked with. What was wrong with it?
Data.project: Take a messy public dataset, clean it, and publish the analysis with its caveats stated.
Data.first_step: Clean one real dataset and write up what you had to decide.

Mobile.probe: What did you have to do differently building for a phone rather than a browser?
Mobile.project: Ship a small app that works offline and syncs when a connection returns.
Mobile.first_step: Build one screen that behaves correctly with no network.

Design.probe: Show me something you designed and tell me what you changed after someone used it.
Design.project: Redesign a flow you find frustrating and document the reasoning behind each change.
Design.first_step: Redesign one screen and write a paragraph on why each change helps.

Other.probe: Tell me about a project where you used this, and what you would do differently.
Other.project: Build something small that genuinely requires this skill, and document the decisions.
Other.first_step: Use it once in a real project rather than a tutorial.

accessibility.probe: How would someone using a keyboard only get through your main flow?
accessibility.project: Audit a project with a screen reader and fix what you find.
accessibility.first_step: Make one flow fully keyboard-navigable and fix its contrast.

agile.probe: How did your team decide what to build next, and what happened when that turned out wrong?
agile.project: Run a project in short iterations with a written backlog and a retrospective.
agile.first_step: Plan your next project in week-long iterations and write down what slipped.

authentication.probe: Walk me through what happens from a user typing a password to them being logged in.
authentication.project: Implement sign-up, login, password reset and session expiry properly in one app.
authentication.first_step: Add real authentication to a project instead of a hardcoded user.

aws.probe: Where does your project run right now, and what would you need to change to run it for real users?
aws.project: Deploy a project with managed storage, a database and environment-based configuration.
aws.first_step: Deploy one finished project to a cloud provider rather than a laptop.

ci/cd.probe: What runs automatically when you push? What would you want to run that does not?
ci/cd.project: Add a pipeline that runs tests and blocks a merge when they fail.
ci/cd.first_step: Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs your tests on every push.

data structures.probe: Tell me about a time you chose one data structure over another. What did it cost?
data structures.project: Implement a structure from scratch and use it in something real.
data structures.first_step: Re-solve three problems you have already solved, optimising for complexity.

docker.probe: Describe how you would containerise the backend you built. What goes in the image, what stays outside it, and why?
docker.project: Containerise an existing project of yours: a Dockerfile, a compose file for its database, and a README showing a one-command start.
docker.first_step: Write a Dockerfile for a project you have already finished and get it running locally.

express.probe: Explain what middleware is doing in a request you have handled. What would break without it?
express.project: Build an API where auth, logging and validation are each their own middleware layer.
express.first_step: Add authentication middleware to an API you have already built.

git.probe: Describe a time your branch conflicted badly with someone else's. What did you do?
git.project: Work through a project using branches and pull requests even while working alone.
git.first_step: Use feature branches and PRs on your next project rather than committing to main.

graphql.probe: What does GraphQL make easier for the client, and what does it move onto the server?
graphql.project: Put a GraphQL layer over an API you already have and handle the N+1 problem it creates.
graphql.first_step: Expose one existing REST resource through a GraphQL schema.

jest.probe: How do you test a component that fetches data? What do you replace, and what do you leave real?
jest.project: Add a test suite covering behaviour rather than implementation, and run it in CI.
jest.first_step: Write tests for one component, including its loading and error states.

jwt.probe: Where do you store a token in the browser, and what attack does each choice expose you to?
jwt.project: Build auth with short-lived tokens, refresh, and a working logout.
jwt.first_step: Add token-based auth to an existing API, including expiry.

kubernetes.probe: You have a container that runs. What problems appear when you need three of them behind one address?
kubernetes.project: Deploy a two-service app to a local cluster with health checks and a rolling update.
kubernetes.first_step: Run a single-service deployment locally and practise updating it without downtime.

linux.probe: Your service is running but not responding. What do you check, in what order?
linux.project: Set up a server yourself: user, firewall, reverse proxy, service manager, logs.
linux.first_step: Deploy a project to a bare VM rather than a managed platform.

machine learning.probe: How did you know your model was actually working, rather than memorising?
machine learning.project: Take a problem end to end: data, baseline, model, evaluation, and an honest write-up of the limits.
machine learning.first_step: Build a baseline model and beat it, documenting both.

microservices.probe: What would you split out of your current project first, and what new problem would that create?
microservices.project: Split one project into two services that communicate, and handle one of them being down.
microservices.first_step: Extract one responsibility from a monolith into its own service.

mongodb.probe: What did you denormalise, and what did that cost you later?
mongodb.project: Build an app whose read patterns genuinely justify a document store, and say why in the README.
mongodb.first_step: Model one feature in a document store and write the queries the screens need.

node.js.probe: Your API makes two slow calls to other services. How would you handle that, and what happens to other requests meanwhile?
node.js.project: Build a REST API with routing, middleware, auth and tests, and document its endpoints.
node.js.first_step: Port a small script you have written into an HTTP service with two or three endpoints.

pandas.probe: Describe the messiest data you have had to clean. What did you have to decide?
pandas.project: Build a reproducible pipeline from raw data to a published result.
pandas.first_step: Clean one real dataset and document every judgement call.

postgresql.probe: Describe a query that was slow. How did you work out why?
postgresql.project: Build a schema with real constraints and foreign keys, then add the indexes your queries need.
postgresql.first_step: Move a project off a document store onto Postgres and write the migrations.

pytest.probe: How would you test code that talks to a database without making the tests slow and flaky?
pytest.project: Build a project with fixtures, parameterised tests and a CI run.
pytest.first_step: Add pytest to an existing script and cover its edge cases.

react.probe: Describe a piece of state in your app that was hard to place. Where did it end up, and why there?
react.project: Build an interface with real data-fetching states: loading, empty, error and success.
react.first_step: Rebuild a static page as components with real state, not just props.

redis.probe: What in your app would you cache, and how would you know when the cache is wrong?
redis.project: Add caching to a slow endpoint and measure the difference honestly.
redis.first_step: Cache one expensive query and handle invalidating it.

responsive design.probe: How do you decide where a layout should break? What do you test on?
responsive design.project: Take a desktop-only project of yours and make it genuinely usable on a phone.
responsive design.first_step: Fix one existing page so it works at 375px wide.

rest api.probe: How did you decide what your endpoints were called and what they returned?
rest api.project: Design and build an API with versioning, pagination and honest error responses.
rest api.first_step: Document an existing API of yours properly, including its error cases.

sql.probe: Write me the shape of a query joining three tables — what order would you filter in, and why?
sql.project: Take a dataset and answer five real questions about it in SQL alone.
sql.first_step: Practise joins and aggregation against a real dataset rather than a tutorial schema.

system design.probe: Your app now has a hundred times the traffic. What breaks first, and how would you know?
system design.project: Write up the architecture of something you built, and what you would change at ten times the scale.
system design.first_step: Document the architecture of your largest project, including its bottlenecks.

testing.probe: What in your project is hardest to test, and why?
testing.project: Take an untested project of yours to meaningful coverage, starting with the parts you most fear changing.
testing.first_step: Write tests for the one function you are most afraid to edit.

typescript.probe: Show me a type you wrote that caught a real bug. What would the JavaScript version have done?
typescript.project: Convert an existing JavaScript project to TypeScript and remove every `any` you add on the way.
typescript.first_step: Add TypeScript to one existing project and type its API responses properly.

vue.probe: How would you structure a form with validation that also needs to warn before discarding changes?
vue.project: Build a small single-page app with routing, a shared store and a real API behind it.
vue.first_step: Rebuild a React or vanilla project you already have in Vue and note what transferred.
